equity_bridge.item: Pension + retiree health liabilities, net of 22% tax
equity_bridge.note: Q2 FY2026 10-Q balance sheet: pension liabilities 77.8 + retiree health care 16.6 = 94.4 pre-tax

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: blend of revenue 3yr (2.1%) and 5yr (5.5%) CAGR, consistent with FY2026 H1 growth of 4.7% incl. FX and acquisitions
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.1% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr CAGR 5.5% and EPS 3yr 4.4%: book value compounds on retained earnings well ahead of the business, so it is not used as the growth proxy. EPS 5yr (11.1%) starts at the COVID FY2020 trough.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = Snap-on-defined FCF (OCF - capex - net finance receivable additions) - SBC - interest income. The 3yr FCF CAGRs start at the FY2022 trough (inventory build + $129M receivable growth) and are meaningless; the 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (1.3%) is below the reported 5yr (2.7%) because interest income rose from $1.7M to $58.8M as cash built up - part of reported FCF growth is cash earning rates, not the business.

scenario_narratives.base: Snap-on keeps compounding as a mid-single-digit grower: the Tools Group van channel stays roughly flat-to-low-growth as technicians favour short-payback items over big-ticket boxes and diagnostics, while Repair Systems & Information and Commercial & Industrial (record 16.8% margin in Q2 FY2026, critical-industries demand, Hi-Force and Diesel Laptops bolt-ons) carry growth of ~3.5% fading to 2.5%. RCI savings and pricing offset tariffs, holding the EBITDA margin at ~28.5%, its FY2023-25 band. Snap-on Credit delinquency stays benign (~1.9% 60+ day). The exit is capped at 16x owner FCF, below the ~20x the market pays today.
scenario_narratives.bull: Rising vehicle age and repair complexity (EV, ADAS) re-accelerate the Tools Group once tariff uncertainty clears, technicians return to big-ticket financed purchases, and C&I keeps double-digit growth with aerospace/defence/power-gen demand and bolt-on M&A into heavy-duty diagnostics. Growth runs 5-5.5% for five years and mix plus RCI lift the EBITDA margin to ~30%. The franchise moat earns an 18x exit, near today's multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: A technician recession: tariffs and a softer labour market push technicians to defer big-ticket purchases and trade down to Matco/Milwaukee, franchisee economics weaken, and Snap-on Credit takes higher losses as delinquencies rise. FY2027 revenue falls 4% (FY2020 fell 3.2% from FY2019; FY2009 fell 15%), stays flat in FY2028, and the margin drops to 26% before recovering only to ~27.3% as premium pricing erodes. Receivable run-off releases some cash in the downturn. Exit at 14x, a mature low-growth industrial multiple.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Snap-on is valued as a mature, moderately cyclical owner-FCF compounder whose captive finance arm is treated as part of the operating business: finance income in the flows, its funding debt in the bridge, receivable growth charged as working capital. SBC is small (~0.6% of revenue) so the house/street band is narrow. Cyclicality is charged in the bear flows and a 20% bear weight, not in the discount rate; terminal values are capped at 14-18x owner FCF, at or below today's ~20x.
key_risks_to_valuation: Tariff-driven technician deferral of big-ticket tool storage and diagnostics purchases persisting into a broader downturn
Credit losses at Snap-on Credit in a labour-market recession (receivables ~$2B vs equity ~$6B)
Trade-down to lower-priced tool-truck and power-tool competitors eroding the price premium
Terminal multiple: the market pays ~20x owner FCF today; the 16x base cap assumes no multiple expansion and part of the gap to price is this choice
Acquisition cadence: bolt-on M&A cash is not in the flows; growth from acquisitions beyond FY2026 is not modelled

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 320.80-423.02
data_sources.financials: SNA_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL API) for revenue, earnings, SBC, interest income, taxes, buybacks; capex, finance receivable additions/collections, debt, cash and diluted shares read from the FY2022, FY2024 and FY2025 10-Ks and the Q2 FY2026 10-Q on SEC EDGAR (CIK 91440)
data_sources.qualitative: SNA_Analysis.json (Q2 FY2026 results, guidance, bull/bear cases)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, Q2 FY2026 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-07-04): 51.7M basic + 0.8M dilutive = 52.5M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging dilution too would double-count). Snap-on is a steady repurchaser ($328.6M FY2025, $191.3M H1 FY2026), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement stock-based compensation add-back $28.9M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation). No combined SBC+equity-award-tax figure is published and no net-share-settlement withholding line appears in financing; option-exercise proceeds ($55.0M FY2022) flow IN, so the add-back is used unadjusted.
inputs.capex_source: Capex is not XBRL-tagged for SNA; read from the 10-K cash flow statements on EDGAR: FY2020 65.6, FY2021 70.1, FY2022 84.2, FY2023 95.0, FY2024 83.5, FY2025 76.0, H1 FY2026 44.3 (vs 42.6). FY2026 guidance ~$100M.
inputs.reported_fcf_definition: Snap-on's own FCF definition: operating cash flow - capex - net additions to finance receivables (additions less collections, investing activities). FY2025: 1,081.7 - 76.0 - (913.6 - 888.9) = 981.0. Owner FCF = 981.0 - SBC 28.9 - interest income 58.8 = 893.3.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~0.9 x 5.0% ERP = ~8.7% cost of equity; $1.2B debt (~6% of capital) at ~4% pre-tax. WACC 8.5%, identical across scenarios: cyclicality and credit risk are charged in the bear flows, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent is already inside operating earnings, so lease cost sits in the EBITDA margin (lease_cost_pct_path 0) and operating lease liabilities ($75.3M non-current) are excluded from net debt. One treatment, no double charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows. NCI earnings ($25.4M FY2025, ~2.5% of NOPAT) are folded into the cash tax driver: 23% cash tax + ~2pp NCI leakage = 25%. NCI equity ($25.0M) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.financial_services_treatment: Snap-on Credit (finance + contract receivables, ~$2B) is an embedded captive lender. It is valued inside the operating flows: its operating income (pre corporate interest) is in consolidated operating earnings and hence the EBITDA margin; the $1.2B of senior notes that fund it are deducted in full in net debt; receivable growth is charged through the negative working-capital capture. Interest income on the $1.6B cash pile sits below operating earnings, so it is outside the flows and the cash is in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical: industrials'). Snap-on is a mature, moderately cyclical US tools/diagnostics manufacturer with a captive finance arm; no REIT/bank/holdco/distress features. The finance arm is not large enough relative to the group (FS revenue $412.9M of $5,156.1M, 8%) to warrant a sum-of-parts with residual income; it is folded into the flows as described in financial_services_treatment. EBITDA margin is defined for the engine as operating earnings (after financial services) + D&A + SBC: FY2023 28.5%, FY2024 28.8%, FY2025 28.2% (1,327.7 + 98.5 + 28.9 = 1,455.1). TIMING: year 1 is the full FY2026, discounted a full year from Oct-2026 against a 2026-07-04 balance sheet; the H1 FY2026 overlap (~$9/share) is smaller than the ~0.75-year over-discounting, so the convention is net conservative. LABEL WARNING: the CSV's 'Q2 2026' and 'Q3 2026' rows are fiscal Q1 and Q2 FY2026 (quarters ended 2026-04-04 and 2026-07-04); Q3 FY2026 is not yet reported. Q2 FY2026 included $159.1M of acquisitions (Hi-Force, Diesel Laptops), already out of the cash balance used here.

base.wc_capture_note: Growth consumes capital: trade receivables + inventory less payables ~33% of revenue plus finance/contract receivables funding technician credit. FY2020-25 receivable additions and WC build absorbed well over 60% of the revenue increase; -60% used.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: FY2026 ETR guidance ~22%; cash tax paid ran $327M in FY2025 (~24% of pre-tax). 23% cash tax + ~2pp NCI leakage.
base.capex_pct_note: FY2026 guided ~$100M (~1.9% of revenue) vs 1.5-1.9% FY2023-25; settles at 1.8%, above PP&E depreciation (~1.5%; D&A 1.9% includes acquired-intangible amortization).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the core Tools Group has been flat for three years, tariffs are a live high-severity risk, and Snap-on Credit ties the downside to technician credit. Base 55%: three decades of steady pricing power and a conservative balance sheet make the middle path the most likely. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both a Tools Group re-acceleration and sustained C&I/margin gains, two independent things going right.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
